recipes.name: Simple and Delicious Beet Greens
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, or to taste
salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add beet greens; cook, uncovered, until tender, about 2 minutes. Drain in a colander.
Immediately immerse greens in ice water for several minutes to stop the cooking process.
Drain well once the greens are cold; coarsely chop.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in garlic and pepper flakes; cook and stir until fragrant, about 1 minute. Stir in chopped greens until coated; season with salt and black pepper. Cook just until greens are hot; 1 to 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple and Delicious Beet Greens
raw_recipe.description: Beet greens have a flavor similar to kale. This simple, 15-minute side dish recipe pairs beet greens with garlic, zesty pepper flakes, and lemon juice.

video.description: Did you know you can eat beet greens? The hearty green leaves that top fresh bundles of beets can actually be used in many of the same ways as kale! In this video, learn how to cook beet greens with garlic and crushed red pepper flakes for a delicious and nutritious side dish. This beet greens recipe is so easy to make and comes together in just 15 minutes. Plus, it makes beets a 2-in-1 purchase, helping you get the most bang for your buck at the grocery store.

review.reviewBody: I just saute in olive oil in a big skillet and skip the blanching part to save washing a pan. First I thinly slice the stems and add them first to get a bit of a head start on the leaves then slice the leaves in thin strips (the bunch at a time). When wilted it is ready.

Beats and the leaves (among many other foods) are high in oxalic acid which causes gout, kidney stones and joint pain. Because oxalates are water soluble, they can be reduced by blanching, boiling, or steaming with the liquid discarded. So don't skip the blanching and make sure you eat it with some calcium (egg, milk, or pill). Fermentation reduces oxalates as well.

I skipped the blanching part, chopped up the stems very small and added sliced fresh mushrooms and some fresh onion plus a dash of garlic powder and black pepper, Sauteed the mushrooms, beet leaf stems and onion for about 10 minutes, then added the chopped leaves. Cooked under a cover for another 10 minutes, added a dash of white vinegar and served over a little brown rice. Delicious and filling .

I just cleaned the beet/kale leaves, cut off hard stems and tore into bite size pieces. I used olive oil and sauteed them slowly, skipping the blanching part. I added in diced onion and bacon crumbles. I will omit the red pepper flakes when I make them again today and use Mrs Dash Spicy instead. I added lots of pepper and some salt. It was a very yummy recipe, my 15 year old couldn't keep his hands out of it!

this was really tasty.. like Wilma Laura Wiggins, i didn't bother blanching the greens.. i just cut them into strips and sauteed them.. i cut the recipe in half and used 1 tsp of bacon grease for the oil and doubled the garlic.. i didn't have fresh lemon so i added a bit of bottled lemon juice as i cooked.. very good.. ty for the recipe

The recipe turns out fine, but I think that all that blanching and washing the leaves will rob them of much of their soluble vitamins. I prefer to chop them, including the tender stems, and saute in olive oil then adding the garlic and pepper flakes and perhaps a splash of vegetable broth.
I blanched the greens using chicken broth. I then added some of the broth to the oil and garlic sauté to keep it a little moister. Delicious!

Delicious! I did not blanch. I sautéed the garlic first in olive oil than sautéed the greens over low - medium heat. They will get soft eventually. Just be careful not to burn. Added some sea salt and a squeeze of lemon. Perfection!
MAKE SURE YOU cook off the liquid. once the greens are cooked push to the outside and turn the heat to high to cook off the liquid
I just sauté the greens. I did not blanch them. I used limes instead of lemons. This was a tasty way to use the greens from my garden.

I've made this several times and enjoy the basic recipe. I do not skip the blanching. Typically skip the lemon and serve for breakfast with a bit of crumbled feta and eggs over medium. Thank you for sharing this. 
I harvested beets from my garden I had an abundance of greens so my picture is of a variation of the recipe. Sauteed garlic, red pepper flakes, onion, bit of leftover bell pepper and mushrooms. Added chopped (blanched) greens and what was left in a bag of spinach. So yummy!
I loved the recipe and followed it as written, then added craisins and chopped pecans to add textures. Will do this again for sure!

In the past,I had always just boiled my beet greens in lightly salted water until stems were tender,drained them,then added butter and salt/pepper. This recipe was a delightful change and gave them a boost of flavor. The only changes I made were using butter vs olive oil to sautée and using a few bits of lemon zest in addition to the lemon juice. I will definitely make these again! ...and so easy too! 😉😘

I never ate roasted beets or beet greens before. I wanted to grow some to try though, and I will be planting more today! I followed the recipe and added some feta to the greens and they are absolutely delicious.
I chopped the tops small and added grated fresh apples. Adding the sweet made this a hit with my kids. This was excellent hot along side a nice pot roast or as a cold slaw the next a burger.
Loved this recipe, twinned it with some breaded chicken and it was a great way to use up something I usually throw away!
A great side dish! Cooked a lil too much but still good!
Skipped the parboil, otherwise cooked as written. Can't believe I made it to 65 without ever cooking beet greens! They were, as your recipe says "Simple and Delicious"!
Makes great sandwiche with lemon sauce and some walnuts

Happy to find this recipe... it sounds super easy and super tasty. I'm looking to incorporate more potassium into my diet, and the best way for our bodies to get the most potassium from beet greens is to cook them. Who knew? With this recipe as my guide, I'm all in!!
